title: Finding the leftmost insertion point with binary search
summary: Keep searching leftward when the midpoint equals the target so as to locate the insertion position before all equal elements.
context: Given the ascending array [1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 10, 12, 15] indexed from 0 to 9, find the insertion point for target = 6. Value 6 occupies indices 2 through 6 consecutively; the problem asks for the index where a new 6 should be inserted so that it appears to the left of all existing 6s (this algorithm only computes and returns the insertion index without actually inserting or shifting elements in the array).

Pointers i and j mark the left and right boundaries of the closed search interval [i, j], and the midpoint index is computed as m = (i + j) / 2 rounded down. When nums[m] < target, set i = m + 1 to advance rightward; when nums[m] > target or nums[m] == target, set j = m - 1 to narrow leftward, keeping pointer j approaching the rightmost element smaller than target and pointer i approaching the first position greater than or equal to target.
description: Each round first computes the midpoint and then moves one boundary. Right after a boundary is updated, m in the figure still shows the previous midpoint and may lie outside the new interval; m is updated only when the midpoint is recomputed.

Below, the fixed input is listed first, followed by a table summarizing the pointer trace across all eight frames, and then step-by-step notes explaining the reason for each action and the resulting state. The eight frames correspond to three rounds of midpoint comparison, not eight loop iterations.

frames.title: Initialize the search interval
frames.explanation: The target value is 6. Initialize i = 0 and j = 9 so that the closed interval [0, 9] covers all ten elements, with m not yet computed; for the array, see “Fixed input: target value 6.”
frames.key_state: Initialization: target 6, i = 0, j = 9, interval [0, 9], m not yet computed.
frames.announcement: Set left boundary i = 0 and right boundary j = 9 so that the closed search interval [0, 9] covers all 10 elements.

frames.title: Compute midpoint 4
frames.explanation: Round 1: with i = 0 and j = 9, compute m = (0 + 9) // 2 = 4 on interval [0, 9]. nums[4] = 6 equals the target, but we cannot yet tell whether it is the leftmost 6.
frames.key_state: Round 1 midpoint: i = 0, j = 9, interval [0, 9], m = 4, nums[4] = 6.
frames.announcement: Compute the first-round midpoint m = (0 + 9) // 2 = 4 on closed interval [0, 9]; midpoint element nums[4] = 6 equals target value 6.

frames.title: Encounter 6, move right boundary left
frames.explanation: nums[4] = 6 equals the target; to check whether more 6s lie to the left, execute j = m - 1. Now i = 0 and j = 3, giving interval [0, 3]; m = 4 in the figure is the unrecomputed old midpoint, left outside the new interval to its right.
frames.key_state: After encountering 6, move right boundary left: i = 0, j = 3, interval [0, 3]; old m = 4 lies outside the interval and has not been recomputed.
frames.announcement: nums[4] = 6 matches the target. Set j = m - 1 = 3 to look for an earlier 6 and find the leftmost insertion point. The figure still shows the old midpoint, m = 4, to the right of [0, 3].

frames.title: Compute midpoint 1
frames.explanation: Round 2: with i = 0 and j = 3, recompute m = (0 + 3) // 2 = 1 on interval [0, 3]. nums[1] = 3 is less than target 6, so the insertion point lies to its right.
frames.key_state: Round 2 midpoint: i = 0, j = 3, interval [0, 3], m = 1, nums[1] = 3, less than target 6.
frames.announcement: Recompute midpoint m = (0 + 3) // 2 = 1 on the new interval [0, 3]; midpoint element nums[1] = 3 is less than target value 6.

frames.title: Encounter 3, move left boundary right
frames.explanation: Because nums[1] = 3 is less than target 6, execute i = m + 1. Now i = 2 and j = 3, giving interval [2, 3]; m = 1 in the figure is the unrecomputed old midpoint, left outside the new interval to its left.
frames.key_state: After encountering 3, move left boundary right: i = 2, j = 3, interval [2, 3]; old m = 1 lies outside the interval and has not been recomputed.
frames.announcement: Because nums[1] = 3 is less than target value 6, the leftmost insertion point must lie to its right, so execute i = m + 1 to move the left boundary right to 2; in the figure, old midpoint m = 1 has not yet been recomputed and remains to the left of the new interval [2, 3].

frames.title: Compute midpoint 2
frames.explanation: Round 3: with i = 2 and j = 3, recompute m = (2 + 3) // 2 = 2 on interval [2, 3]. nums[2] = 6 again equals the target.
frames.key_state: Round 3 midpoint: i = 2, j = 3, interval [2, 3], m = 2, nums[2] = 6.
frames.announcement: Recompute midpoint m = (2 + 3) // 2 = 2 on interval [2, 3]; midpoint element nums[2] = 6 again equals target value 6.

frames.title: Encounter 6 again, interval becomes empty
frames.explanation: Because nums[2] = 6 equals the target, again execute j = m - 1. Now i = 2 and j = 1, so the closed interval [2, 1] is empty and the loop is about to end; the figure still keeps old midpoint m = 2 without recomputing it.
frames.key_state: After encountering 6 again: i = 2, j = 1, interval [2, 1] is empty; old m = 2 in the figure is not recomputed.
frames.announcement: Because nums[2] = 6 equals target value 6, execute j = m - 1 again to get j = 1; now i = 2 is greater than j = 1, making the closed search interval empty and satisfying the loop termination condition.

frames.title: Return leftmost insertion index 2
frames.explanation: The loop ends, and the figure keeps only the returned pointer i = 2 while hiding j and m. Index 2 is where a new 6 would go, before all five existing 6s; no insertion or element shifting takes place in the original array.
frames.key_state: Search complete, returning leftmost insertion index i = 2; j and m are no longer shown, and the original array is unchanged.
frames.announcement: The loop terminates because the interval is empty and returns left-boundary index i = 2, the position to the left of all five existing 6s where a new 6 belongs; this algorithm only computes and returns the insertion index without modifying or shifting elements in the original array.
